chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn Uthman from Shu'ayb ibn Ya'qub al-Aqarqufi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He was asked, and I was sitting with him listening, about the divorce of a male slave. He said, 'He has no divorce and no marriage. Do you not hear Allah, the Exalted, saying, "A slave who is unable to do anything"?'
He said, 'He is unable to have divorce and marriage except with the permission of his master.'
So if a questioner asks about the report that was narrated...
ai.seo_question: Does a male slave need his master's permission for marriage and divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a male slave lacks independent legal capacity for marriage and divorce, interpreting the Quranic phrase 'unable to do anything' (4:3) as specifically referring to these familial contracts requiring the master's consent. This ruling underscores the hierarchical nature of the master-slave relationship in Shia jurisprudence, where the slave's personal status is contingent upon the owner's authority.
